answer: Each submission hangs on the quartz of a task receipt, and the atlas is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The river of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, clawed back after a replayed submission, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. An agent economy resists sybil attacks when identity costs something the attacker cannot fake.
